about_the_game:
What is this even?

LoFinosaurs takes inspiration from looping LoFi nature videos I would put on my living room TV. I loved the relaxing ambient visuals and noise they brought into my home. Sometimes I'd catch myself after who knows how long staring at this captivating loop; wishing it wasn't a just a loop.

Wouldn't it be cool if there was a whole world like that to lazily explore? A world full of creatures going about their lives. A world with sunrises and sunsets, sunny days and drizzly mornings, lightning bugs and leaves. I wanted a beautiful, dynamic, nature scape to put on my screen where every frame is as beautiful as the best LoFi loop you can find. Also, I wanted there to be dinosaurs, because I love them.

Captivating gameplay, player optional

LoFinosaurs is designed to be a relaxing, no pressure experience. No losing, no lives, no failure conditions. That's not to say there are not moments of excitement. T-Rexs have to eat after all, but they won't be eating you.

This "game" is designed to be played at your leisure and takes care of itself when you put the controller down. I put "game" in quotes because I'm not entirely sure it is a game. It's kind of a mix of a coloring book, a video game, and a digital paludarium. Whatever it is, I think it's neat.

To support this type of "game" there are a couple of ways to play. From most active to passive, we've got:

  • I wanna do it: Take direct control with a mouse or gamepad and explore the world with simple point and click controls.

  • One button dopamine hit: Tap spacebar or right bumper to automatically move to and recolor a new target. Tap tap tap, new meadow who this?

  • Look Ma, no hands: After a few second with no input, Squishy the dragonfly will dutifully continue the work of recoloring the landscape according to the colors you have chosen.

LoFi dinos, HiFi simulation

These aren't your typical "wander here and there and wait to be killed or tamed" background dinosaurs (Looking at you Ark). These dinos have needs, and their needs influence their behavior. Under the hood they have:

  • Hunger (Big whoop)

  • Thirst (Duh)

  • Energy (Ok)

  • Age (Hmm)

  • Social (I could see that being cool)

  • Antisocial (I get it)

  • Territory (This is mine now)

So, when you a see pretty colored Brachiosaur ambling along in the distance. It could be a pretty colored, tired, old, thirsty Brachiosaur, trying to figure out if it is worth leaving the rest of the herd to get a drink and maybe a soak before it needs to head home to the nest for the night.

Herds have alphas and the alphas dictate in general, where the herd is going to be. If there are babies, generally the herd will stick close to its nesting grounds. When the babies are grown enough, the alpha might lead a migration to a distant part of the island. Some species prefer to be in tight packed herds. Some like to spread out a bit but still be able to see each other. Some species only herd when they have young or eggs. Regardless of species, some individuals will have needs that supersede its desire to be close to its friends and it will strike out on its own...or finish its nap and catchup later.

Being a nature sim, there is death too. Dino's can die to old age, predation, drowning, or fighting to defend or usurp alpha status or territory. Like in nature, death brings new life. Herd sizes are self-balancing and when a herd member dies, an egg will be laid. That's your opportunity to select new colors for the species, allowing you to breed that cotton candy colored triceratops herd you've always dreamed of.

How much game is in here?

I plan to launch with at least 10 interactable species with full dynamic behaviors on a 6-kilometer island. So far I've added:

  • T-Rex (We have a T-Rex!)

  • Brachiosaurus (It's...It's a dinosaur!)

  • Ankylosaurus (No brainer.)

  • Gallimimus (They're uh... flocking this way!)

For sure adding:

  • Utahraptor (You've bred raptors?)

  • Triceratops (The most beautiful thing I ever saw.)

  • Parasaurolophus (The one with the pompadour...Elvis.)

I haven't decided on the others yet. Feel free to suggest some in the discord linked on this page.

There are also various non-interactable creatures for ambience such as fish, small dinosaurs (compys), pterosaurs, and a few large one-of-a-kind creatures that you'll encounter from time to time. The island is a single biome (Subtropical) with sub biomes like marshes, meadows, jungle, bamboo forest, etc. Complete with a day and night cycle and dynamic weather.

Plans for more content?

I'd like to add even more species and a full underwater ecosystem at some point, but that depends on the interest in this game as is. I'm a solo developer and I can't really continue work on a product that doesn't pay my bills. That said, you might catch glimpses of life in the ocean other than fish if you're lucky. If people like this, I'll keep adding to it. It's a fun project.

pc_requirements.minimum:
Minimum:
  • OS: Windows 10
  • Processor: Intel i5-2300 or AMD Phenom II 830
  • Memory: 8 GB RAM
  • Graphics: NVIDIA GeForce GTX 950 or AMD Radeon RX 460
  • DirectX: Version 11
  • Storage: 2 GB available space
pc_requirements.recommended:
Recommended:
  • OS: Windows 10 or 11
  • Processor: Intel i5-8300H or AMD Ryzen 3 2300U
  • Graphics: NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1060 or AMD Radeon RX 580
  • DirectX: Version 12
  • Storage: 2 GB available space

short_description: A relaxing simulation game where you play as a dragonfly exploring a vibrant world filled with colorful dinosaurs. Recolor the world around you, collect dinosaur nests, and discover scenic viewpoints in a handcrafted world. Experience the beauty at your own pace, whether actively or in idle mode.
